chunks: And from him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who wishes to travel in Ramadan. He said: 'If he morning-prays in his town and then departs, then if he wishes, he may fast, and if he wishes, he may break his fast.'

key_terms.أَصْبَحَ: He morninged / performed the morning prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler in Ramadan who has already prayed Fajr in their home town before leaving?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific condition under which a traveler retains the option (*khiyar*) to fast or break their fast in Ramadan: they must have performed the morning prayer (*Salat al-Fajr*) in their place of residence before departing. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the location of the morning prayer as the determinant for establishing the 'residence' status, thereby allowing flexibility even if the journey begins immediately after dawn.
